newsitem.title: USA: Ford boosts sport utility production at Michigan Truck.
newsitem.headline: Ford boosts sport utility production at Michigan Truck.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Thursday it will stop making F-Series pickup trucks at its Michigan Truck Plant later this month so the facility can make full-size sport utility vehicles exclusively.

The move will coincide with the start of production of the new Lincoln Navigator in May. Ford has not set a formal production launch yet for the Navigator, a luxury version of the popular Expedition, said spokesman Mike Vaughn.

The Navigator is due to go on sale July 1. Ford has said it expects to sell 30,000 Navigators a year. The change will allow Ford to make 282,000 Expeditions and Navigators a year, up 28,000 units from the previous production mix.

Michigan Truck, the only plant that makes the full-size sport utility vehicles, began production of the Expedition last July. Since then, it has made more than 150,000 of the popular vehicles, one of the most profitable for Ford.

"The Expedition is now a clear leader in its segment, and we believe initial demand for the Lincoln Navigator indicates another winner," said Jacques Nasser, president of Ford Automotive Operations, in a statement.

All 1997 model year F-Series pickup production lost at Michigan Truck due to the change will be made up through overtime work on weekdays and Saturdays at other Ford truck plants now producing the F-Series.
Ford makes the F-Series trucks at plants in Norfolk, Va., Oakville Ontario, and Kansas City.

Ford said it is studying how to make up lost production of F-Series on a long-term basis, once 1998 model production begins this summer. If market conditions change, Ford said it will be able to return F-Series production to Michigan Truck within 90 days.
